reader.requirement: A relative WRITE, successful or not, must leave the file position indicator where the last OPEN, START or READ put it, so a following READ NEXT continues from that position (and picks up a record inserted after it).
reader.edition-search: RelativeConnector.Write sets only _lastReleasedSlot (sequential) and _lastSlot; it never touches FpiValid or the FPI key. grep Edition|DialectBehavior in RelativeConnector.cs finds only the out-of-range key gate, which does not touch the FPI.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness sets the FPI by a random READ and writes one higher key; a START-set indicator, a lower inserted key and a failed WRITE are not exercised

probes.expected: START at 4 then WRITE 3: READ NEXT gives 4; a failed WRITE (22) and a WRITE of 5 leave the indicator at 4: next are 5, 6, 8, 10, end

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR5  (4.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR5

reader.notes: The WRITE path has no FPI assignment at all; the probe shows a START-set and READ-set indicator survive both a successful and a failed WRITE.

refuter.evidence: rfpi.cob at --std 85, aimed at the OPEN-set and the AT-END-set indicator the reader did not try: records 5,6,8; OPEN I-O sets the FPI to 1 (§1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR10), WRITE 2 then READ NEXT -> 002 REC002 (selected by GR4c of READ, so the WRITE did not move the FPI to the first existing record); after READ NEXT reached AT END (10), WRITE 9 -> 00, READ NEXT -> 46 (the FPI still says no next record; record 9 not returned). DELETE/WRITE of 5 between READs: READ NEXT continues 5, 6, 8. cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR5; OK §1985:VIII.4.4.4 GR10 'the file position indicator is set to 1'; OK §1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR4.
